Run-in: the stock is -58% from its 52-week high of 87.88. It slid from 46.52 before the August print to 31.10 at Friday's close (2026-11-20), much of the last fortnight with a very weak tape (SPY -4.4% on 11-05 and -3.6% on 11-20). Short interest is 17.54M shares, 31.6% of float, about 10 days to cover (Nasdaq settlement 2026-10-30, Yahoo key statistics). Consensus (Yahoo earningsTrend today): FQ4 revenue $774.4M (range 763-783, 17 analysts) against a guide of $760-780M, adjusted EBITDA guide $100-105M; FQ1 FY27 revenue $822.0M (range 794-866, 13 analysts), which is +6.1% on the FQ4 consensus; FY27 $3.61B; FY27 EPS cut from 0.77 to 0.73 over 90 days. Known and dated: the Walmart expansion of 2026-10-29 (8-K: about $6B initial commitment, up to $6.92B of backlog, $125M development funding, plus a restriction on selling to one specified company), after which the stock fell 4.0% that day; the cellumation acquisition (2026-10-13); the CFO's August remarks that FQ4 starts would be in line with or just below FQ3's 11, gross margin flat to slightly below 25%, the next-generation storage inflection 'in the second half of next year', and positive FCF expected in FQ4.
view: Symbotic's FY26 guidance record is consistent. Each quarter it guides the midpoint about 5% above the last actual and lands at or just above the top: Q1 $630.0M against 610-630, Q2 $676.5M against 650-670, Q3 $720.8M against 700-720. So FQ4 likely prints around $780-790M with EBITDA at the top of 100-105, and the reported quarter is not where the reaction is decided. The line is the FQ1 FY27 guide, together with how management frames FY27 now that the Walmart expansion has taken backlog to about $29B. Two kinds of evidence point opposite ways on that guide. For the street's +6% Q1: the Q3 10-Q says about 15% of the $22.5B RPO is recognised in the next 12 months, about $3.4B, which implies an average of roughly $880M a quarter of systems revenue over FQ4-FQ3 FY27. For a softer Q1: last year's FQ1 guide was flat sequentially (610-630 against a $618M FQ4), and the street modelled that ($611.5M). The CFO also said in August that starts are flat to down, that revenue arrives 'closer to month 13 forward', that the storage-structure inflection is a second-half FY27 event, and that revenue per deployment has fallen for four quarters. A repeat of the usual +5% step from a ~$785M FQ4 gives a midpoint around $820-825M, on top of consensus. A flatter, seasonal Q1 gives $790-805M, a miss of 2-4%. The last two guides, both in-line-ish '+5%' steps, drew -7.7% and -14.9%. Against that, the short is crowded (31.6% of float), so a clean guide plus a $29B backlog, positive FCF and any new non-Walmart customer could squeeze as in November 2025 (+39%). Today's 16.5% rally, about 6 points beyond beta, has already spent some of that fuel. Net, I lean slightly down, but the deciding number is not visible and I cannot show the street is wrong about Q1. This is not a bet.

recommendation.reason: The print turns on the FQ1 FY27 guide against a $822M consensus that assumes +6% sequential growth. Last year's Q1 guide was flat sequentially and management's August comments put the ramp in the second half of FY27, which leans slightly toward a soft guide. But the RPO arithmetic supports the street, the company has beaten the top of every FY26 range, and a 31.6%-of-float short makes any good surprise move the stock a long way. Nothing I found is dated after the company last spoke and moves one side of the guide clearly beyond what consensus holds, so the evidence is short of 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: An FQ1 revenue guide with a midpoint at or above about $825M plus positive FQ4 free cash flow (or a named new non-Walmart customer) would make the up case likely through a squeeze. A guide midpoint at or below about $805M would confirm the lean down.

self_critique: The down lean rests on one analogy, last year's flat Q1 guide, and on CFO phrasing about second-half timing. Last year's Q1 may have been flat for reasons that do not repeat (the FQ4 FY25 base was itself a jump), and the RPO note implies a ramp that supports the consensus. A short of 31.6% of float, a stock 58% off its high, many downgrades already taken, and a management that can now cite about $29B of backlog and positive FCF make an upside squeeze as plausible as a guide disappointment. Against my lean, today's tape is very risk-on and a beta-1.4 name can move several points overnight on futures alone. So 45 is about as far from 50 as the evidence allows.
approach_notes: P6 (taking the run-in apart against QQQ, and finding the line in the last reactions) was the most useful part and kept me from reading today's +16.5% as company news. P7's push to estimate the unseen guide from its inputs helped frame the question, but here the inputs conflict (RPO arithmetic against seasonality and management timing), and the playbook gives no way to settle conflicting inputs other than staying near 50.
